<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **187** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1aab83e008917f501af2fcee095f67a62ce4f6b3` — the merge of head `80a79c7732c04fc57b067c26aa74bdabe5b34604` into base `6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1aab83e008917f501af2fcee095f67a62ce4f6b3 && git checkout 1aab83e008917f501af2fcee095f67a62ce4f6b3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb 80a79c7732c04fc57b067c26aa74bdabe5b34604 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb && git merge --no-ff 80a79c7732c04fc57b067c26aa74bdabe5b34604

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80a79c7732c04fc57b067c26aa74bdabe5b34604`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts + packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #36794 (body, triage 7118224568, claim 7192981274, amendment 7194794693), the PR body and its 17-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `061e3422`), and the check-runs on the head. Newest run per check name is success or skipped; the cancelled PR-body guards run is superseded by a success on the same head. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. The PR is still a draft.

- `FieldErrorCode` gains one member, `reference_out_of_scope`. The accept-set of `FieldErrorSchema.code` (closed, ADR-0114 D2) widens by one and nothing leaves it. Right, and declared.
- `ValidateDataIssueSchema` gains an optional `scope`, an array of `{ field, value }`, both strings. The element is shared, so the key parses at every position that embeds it: `ImportRowResult.errors` and `.warnings`, the validate verdict's `errors` and `warnings`, and the write answers' `warnings`. The regenerated references show exactly those positions, `api/ValidateDataIssue:scope` enters `authorable-surface/api.json`, and the strictness-ledger count for `api/` moves by one for the nested object. Right. `rule` and `severity` reached this element the same way.
- `BUILTIN_VALIDATION_MESSAGES` gains `import_reference_out_of_scope` in en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES, overridable under `validation.field.import_reference_out_of_scope`. Additive. Right.
- `@objectstack/core` exported types gain two optional members, `RefMatch.scopeDenied` and `FieldCoerceError.scope`. Additive. Right.
- `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` gains one `foreign-vocabulary` row, worded as its three sibling rows. Right.
- Behaviour, not shape: the importer emits the new code where it emitted `reference_not_found` with a qualified sentence, and a scoped read the field-predicate guard refused is no longer probed. Judged in ③ and ④.
- No removal, no tombstone, no rename, no requirement tightened. Nothing implies an ADR-0087 registry entry.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/core` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch. `Metadata-protocol: added` grades the package that carries the key at least minor, and that package is spec. Core publishes a behaviour change and two optional type members, runtime a ledger row; neither carries a protocol key, so patch. `packages/rest` changes a test only and takes no bump. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. The line is right: the diff widens a published enum and a published element, and takes nothing away (see ③ for the narrowing question).
- `added` instead of the card's expected `none` is the gate's own reading of the new authorable-surface row; the claim amendment 7194794693 records the change. Right as declared.
- The changeset body names the case that moved, what stays, and what a client does about it.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The card's question: is moving the cross-parent case out of `reference_not_found` a narrowing for a client that matches by code?** No, not in the declaration's sense. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone is the right line. No `(narrowing)` arm and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

- The arm reads the published accept-set and public surface. After this diff every value that parsed before still parses: `reference_not_found` stays a member, and the issue element only gains an optional key. Nothing is removed, tombstoned or refused, and no requirement tightens.
- What moves is which member the importer EMITS for one case. On an answer position that is one event seen from two sides. The set of codes a client must know grows by one, which is the widening already declared. The client that matched the old code for that case stops matching it. The second effect is real, but it takes no declared capability away: the spec on `main` declares `reference_not_found` as "a lookup target that does not exist", and in the moved case the target exists. Only prose said the cross-master case answers the old code (`import-mappings.mdx` on `main`, and the skill line #37590 tracks), and prose follows the implementation.
- The arm pair is closed and a line takes at most one arm. `(narrowing)` marks a changeset BREAKING and puts the PR on the declared-narrowing leg; here it would describe a diff that refuses no input it accepted before.
- ADR-0087's ledger registers retirements and conversions of what an author can write or a consumer can import. A wire answer is not stored metadata, so there is no FROM and TO a conversion could replay. Its registration gate is driven by a breaking declaration, and none is owed.
- What the move does owe is a plain statement where a consumer reads it. The changeset carries it: the case that moved, the case that stays, and "match both" for a client that wants every unresolved lookup cell. In this repository the one reader keyed on this code for import rows is the Import Wizard, and its fall-through shows the server's sentence until PR-2.
- Treating a re-partition of an answer code as breaking, as a class, would be a rule change for the maintainer. This record does not make it.

**Other flags.**

- The `scope` key, decided by the thread inside ruling A's surface: judged in ④ under `protocol.zod.ts`. It holds.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #37590`: the card is open and names the line this PR makes false. `skills/**` is governed, so the fix belongs there. Right arm.
- Between PR-1 and PR-2: read `formatDryRunError` on the head. A code it has no `case` for falls through to the server's sentence. No regression; the interim text says more than the "no matching record" it replaces.
- `Part of #36794` is right: the Wizard half is PR-2.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no read. The unscoped probe is #36735's: one resolver call per FAILING scoped cell, each candidate one `findData` with an equality `where` and `limit: 2`, pushed to the driver. No id list is materialised and nothing is joined in the application. On the refused path the diff removes reads: the loop stops at the first candidate and the probe is skipped. A miss is still not cached, as the resolver's own comment says on purpose, so a file whose every row names a missing value under a scope pays the probe per row; that is not new here.
- The in-scope extra fix (a caller who cannot read the scoping field keeps `reference_not_found`, and no unscoped probe runs): judged in ④ under `import-runner.ts`. It holds on every door I could reach by reading.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`** — holds. The member sits beside its two siblings, as ruling A item 1 asks. Its comment states the implemented condition: a scoped miss plus an unscoped match answers the new code, and a value matching nothing anywhere keeps the old one. Its first consumer is `coerceError` in `import-coerce.ts`, whose `code` parameter is typed by this enum. Tried to break it: an unscoped match is necessarily outside the scope, because the scoped read over the same candidates has just missed. A record whose scoping field is empty is outside the scope too; the comment's first clause covers it and its gloss "under another parent" overstates it slightly. Accepted.

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** — holds, the route decision included. Ruling A item 2 requires the Wizard to name the scoping column and its cell while it keys on the code and parses no server prose. On `main` the element carries no column at all. The other route, a client deriving the scope from field metadata, would re-implement the inferred-master rule that only the server owns (`referenceScopeSources`), and the docs say the record picker has no counterpart for it. So the key is pulled by the ruling's own acceptance, sits inside ruling A's surface, and is the smaller route. The shape is right: `field` is the row column's API name, which a client maps to its own label, and `value` is the cell as typed. The target-side `param` and the coerced id stay unpublished, and the entries carry only what the caller wrote. Emission agrees with the describe sentence by sentence: only on that code (coerce sets it on the out-of-scope branch alone, the runner copies it only when set, and its absence on `reference_not_found` is pinned), and in the sentence's order (one `scopedBy` array feeds both). First consumer is PR-2's `formatDryRunError`. It reads the row's first-error keys today, and `scope` rides on `errors[]` only, so PR-2 reads element 0, which names the same cell by `ImportRowResultSchema`'s own rule.

**`packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts`** — holds. The key exists in all four locales with both placeholders, and the English render is byte-identical to the sentence #36735 shipped; both are pinned. The jsdoc agrees with `referenceNotFound`: the qualifier is composed from labels, cells and punctuation only.

**`packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`** — agrees with the contract. `referenceNotFound` returns the plain refusal when there is no scope, returns it again before the probe when the scoped match says `scopeDenied`, and otherwise asks once more without the scope through the same resolver. A match or a tie answers the new code, the new sentence key and the `scope` entries. The single-value and multi-value branches both hand in the scoped match.

**`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`** — agrees with the contract. `isScopeFieldDenial` reads the refusal's declared `details`, never its message. Read against the three throw sites on the head that answer that reason (`plugin-security` `predicate-guard.ts`, `plugin-audit` `parent-field-query-guard.ts`, `plugin-approvals` `payload-predicate-guard.ts`): each sets `details` to the object, the bare names of every offending field, and the reason, and the security middleware rethrows the same instance. The candidate list starts at `id`, so the first scoped read reaches the guard and the loop stops there. The refusal is not cached. One site copies `scope` onto the row, and it runs before the dry-run split, so a dry run and a commit answer alike.
Doors: `runImport` has five callers on the head (the REST import route, the REST import-job route, the user-import door, connector pull and datasource pull). All take the resolver built inside `runImport`, none builds a second one, and the REST routes return `summary.results` verbatim. So the fix holds on the dry run and on the commit, over REST and in-process. Which context each caller hands the runner is not in this diff.

**`packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`** — agrees. The row is the sibling rows' wording with the new code, and the vocabulary gate is green on the head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, each an accepted deviation or a follow-up; none moves the verdict:

- Sibling text still describes a cell error as the triple `field`, `code`, `message`: the `ImportRowResultSchema.errors` describe and jsdoc in `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts` (not in this diff), and the `errors` jsdoc near `import-runner.ts:90`. Neither says "only", so neither is false; both are now incomplete. Fixing either moves the head, so it waits for a change that touches those files.
- The "scope was never asked" rule is a positive match on one refusal reason. Any other throw on every scoped candidate is still read as a miss and probed. The one reachable instance I found needs a declaration the platform cannot execute: a `dependsOn` `param` naming a field the engine refuses to filter by (a formula). Lint's `dependsOn` rule judges that the name exists on the referenced object, not that it can be filtered by, and the record picker's filter on the same declaration is refused as well. Each scoped row then answers the new code although the scope was never evaluated. The qualified sentence has said the same since #36735, so the misattribution is not new, but a code now asserts it. The fix belongs at the producer (lint refuses such a `param`), and the resolver could report "could not ask" for any scoped read where no candidate query completed. Follow-up card.
- The guard pin builds the refusal by hand, and no pin drives a real guard through a real engine on the import path. The reason is matched as a string literal across packages, so a rename at the guard would leave the pin green. Follow-up: one real-engine pin.
- For the lane seat, prose not reviewed under ④: `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` says the cell error "names that parent's columns in `scope`" directly after "another parent". `scope` names the row's own columns. A prose-face fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-zt8cu4`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 80a79c7732 · card #36794 (PR-1 of 2) · area s2-data · 2026-11-26T15:11Z

**L1 checklist**
- Shape and relation: `l1-face.mjs --pr 37567` flagged two items, both answered here.
  - `changeset` for `@objectstack/rest`: its one file is `src/import-integration.test.ts`, and the package publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only, so no rest entry is owed.
  - `all-checks`: the one non-success is a cancelled `PR-body guards` run at 14:26:54Z, superseded by the same-name run that succeeded at 14:27:11Z.
  - At 80a79c7732 every newest run per name is success or an expected skip, with 0 pending. 343 changed lines, not governed.

  - N2, a `dependsOn` `param` naming a field the engine will not filter by, and N3, one real-engine pin for the field-guard path: both go on the card as PR-2 scope or a follow-up card at PR-2's ACCEPT.

Tier: S. Landing: ready + auto-merge by this stroke.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [45846812886](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/45846812886) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (5/10)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/45846812886/job/140004129792)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```
  @objectstack/cli:test:  FAIL   integration  test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts > #30120 — with the image switch on, a start missing its settings refuses > none set: exit 1, naming al
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/cli:test: Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
